title: Protocol for generating protoplasts from the leafcutter ant symbiotic fungus Leucoagaricus gongylophorus
author: Stelate, Shik

steps.title: Grow fungal culture on PDA
steps.instruction: Inoculate Leucoagaricus gongylophorus onto potato dextrose agar plates under sterile, axenic conditions; incubate in the dark at 25 °C for three weeks until the colony margin shows active hyphal growth (≈0.5 cm diameter) and the colony center appears dense, white, and fluffy. Avoid overgrown or nutrient‑depleted plates.

steps.title: Wash harvested tissue in osmotic buffer
steps.instruction: Immediately before protoplast isolation, gently wash the harvested hyphal and gongylidia tissue with fresh osmotic stabilization buffer to remove residual medium and extracellular matrix; the washed mycelia may be kept in the same buffer at 4 °C for up to 2 h before digestion.

steps.title: Prepare osmotic stabilization buffer
steps.instruction: Make fresh osmotic stabilization buffer, pre‑equilibrate it to the digestion temperature (25 °C), and verify its osmotic strength by testing a small aliquot for lack of immediate swelling or lysis. The buffer can be prepared in larger batches (e.g., 50 mL) and stored at 4 °C for up to one week.

steps.title: Prepare fresh enzyme solution
steps.instruction: Prepare 2 mL of enzyme cocktail immediately before use; this volume is sufficient for 2 mg of wet mycelial tissue. Keep the mixture at 25 °C until it is added to the fungal material and avoid any freeze–thaw cycles.

steps.title: Sterilize and assemble consumables
steps.instruction: Sterilize and assemble all required consumables, including filtration meshes or sterile nylon cloth, wide‑bore pipette tips, and centrifuge tubes. Consumables can be prepared in advance and stored at 20 °C until needed.

steps.title: Calibrate equipment and set incubation conditions
steps.instruction: Calibrate centrifuges and set up a shaker or incubator to the digestion temperature (25 °C) and the appropriate agitation speed. Confirm rotor compatibility with the planned sample volume and tube type to prevent loss of protoplasts during centrifugation.

steps.title: Excise and wash hyphal tissue
steps.instruction: Using sterile tools, excise actively growing hyphae from three‑week‑old cultures (≈15 mg harvested). Transfer the hyphal fragments into sterile osmotic buffer, then wash gently until no visible medium remains, yielding roughly 2 mg of wet, cleaned fungal material.

steps.title: Digest tissue with enzyme cocktail
steps.instruction: Add the 2 mL freshly prepared enzyme solution to the 2 mg of washed hyphal tissue in osmotic buffer. Incubate at 25 °C with gentle shaking (as set in step 6) for the time required for cell‑wall digestion (as determined empirically).

steps.title: Filter digestion mixture to collect protoplasts
steps.instruction: Pass the digestion mixture through a sterile filtration mesh or nylon cloth to separate liberated protoplasts from undigested debris, collecting the filtrate that contains the protoplast suspension.

steps.title: Wash and purify protoplasts by low‑speed centrifugation
steps.instruction: Clarify the filtrate by low‑force centrifugation at 100 × g for 1 min using a swinging‑bucket rotor (or by gravity sedimentation). Carefully discard the supernatant and gently resuspend the pale, translucent pellet in fresh osmotic buffer. Repeat the wash‑resuspend cycle 2–3 times until residual enzymes are minimized.

steps.title: Quantify protoplast concentration
steps.instruction: Dilute the protoplast suspension 1:1000 and load 200 µL per well in triplicate onto the Ocelloscope system. Recorded counts were 58,769 ± 11,274 cells per 200 µL for the first sample and 67,393 ± 3,216 cells per 200 µL for the second, corresponding to ≈5.9 × 10⁸ and 6.7 × 10⁸ protoplasts per 2 mL of the original undiluted suspension.

steps.title: Assess protoplast viability
steps.instruction: Examine 15 independent microscopy fields (each 250 µm²) after staining with Trypan Blue. Count viable (unstained) and non‑viable (blue‑stained) cells using the Cell Counter plugin in ImageJ, then calculate viability percentage as the proportion of unstained cells relative to the total count.
